newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada union in escalating strike against GM.
newsitem.headline: Canada union in escalating strike against GM.

text.p: More than 15,000 unionized workers at General Motors Corp.'s Canadian unit were off the job on Thursday after beginning a strike the night before that could shut down all GM Canada operations by October 9.

The union began a so-called "escalating" strike against GM less than two hours before Wednesday's midnight strike deadline, after GM delivered a last-minute package that Canadian Auto Workers president Buzz Hargrove called an "insult."
"So we are on strike," Hargrove said. "Our plants are down."
Analysts said last week that a full strike by the company's 26,000 unionized workers in Canada could cost GM $100 million to $150 million a week.
Hargrove called GM's last-minute economic offer a "total joke" crafted by executives at GM headquarters in Detroit.
He said he gave GM Canada chief negotiator Dean Munger the "opportunity to withdraw" the offer before the union's caucus meeting at 10 a.m. Thursday (1400 GMT).
Talks continued on Thursday in Toronto, but Hargrove said the two sides remain "worlds apart" on the major issue of outsourcing and a work-time and work-rule issues.

The strike immediately halted production at GM's Oshawa, Ontario, and Ste-Therese, Quebec, assembly plants. Other GM Canada facilities will join the strike from October 6. If there is no deal, all Canadian operations will be shut by October 9.
Munger said the strike would have a "severe impact" on GM Canada's operations but declined to say when the U.S. operations could be affected.
He acknowledged the union's rejection of the package. "They indicated they weren't happy with it," he said. "We're going to go back and re-evaluate their comments."
GM said earlier a strike in Canada will not affect talks with the United Auto Workers in the United States. "We're working pretty much independently," said spokesman Gerry Holmes.
